tools.name: exec

format.definition:
start: pragma_source | plain_source
pragma_source: PRAGMA_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

PRAGMA_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @exec:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: clock
tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.

tools.name: sleep
tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.2-sol`: Fast, go-to model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority, ultrafast.
- `gpt-6.2-astra`: Our most capable model for complex coding and professional work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority, ultrafast.
- `gpt-6.1-terra`: Efficient model that excels at visual understanding and computer use. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Previous generation model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority, ultrafast.
- `gpt-6-astra`: Previous generation model for complex coding and professional work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority, ultrafast.
- `gpt-6-sol`: Legacy model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-luna`: Fast and affordable model for easier tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-5.6-sol`: Legacy model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-5.6-terra`: Legacy balanced model for agentic coding. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-5.6-luna`: Legacy fast model for simpler tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-5.5`: Legacy coding model. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh. Service tiers: priority.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: mcp__cua_repl
tools.description: UI automation through cua_repl using the initialized cua API.

tools.name: js
tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` selects an existing tab. `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

If the user specifies an app to use, get the app by name, bundle ID, or path:

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp("Example App");
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

Each `cua_repl.js` call opens or continues a browser activity. Keep consecutive calls together. The activity stays open across messages until you emit completion commentary.

**Manual takeover takes priority over the table below.** For a required manual browser step, call the documented takeover API before asking the user to act, unless takeover is already pending. Explain the required step in your final reply. Tab marking alone does not transfer control. While waiting for the user to finish and return control, emit no completion and make no CUA calls, even when answering side questions. The takeover API returning does not end this wait. When the user returns or unblocks you, resume browser work and apply the table. If they cancel, replace, or no longer need the browser work, close the activity before answering, even without another CUA call.

Completion is a standalone assistant commentary message containing only `::browser-complete{title="<headline>"}`. Never put it in a tool call or final reply. Use 3–6 words starting with a past-tense verb to describe the observed outcome. Omit identifiers.

After a user cancels pending browser work: commentary `::browser-complete{title="Stopped browser work"}`, then the final acknowledgement. No browser call is needed.

For an open browser activity:

| Next action                                   | Required output order                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Another CUA call                              | Continue without completion.                                                              |
| A non-CUA tool, final reply, or chat question | Finish required tab marking, emit completion, then take that action in the same response. |

With no open activity, emit no completion. Later CUA use requires a fresh completion at the next table boundary.

If you need a one-time sign-in code, information, or confirmation from the user, follow the table and ask in chat. One-time code entry alone does not require takeover. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

code.description: JavaScript to execute using the initialized cua_repl runtime.

timeout_ms.description: Optional execution timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds) when omitted.

title.description: Short user-facing description of what this code block is doing. Prefer a few words in present-progressive form, such as 'Checking the mobile layout' or 'Comparing prices', over imperative or past-tense titles.

tools.name: js_reset
tools.description: Reset the persistent cua_repl JavaScript session. All JavaScript bindings are discarded. The next cua_repl.js call initializes a fresh runtime for the enabled surfaces. This does not close browser tabs or native apps, or erase their state. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/Users/alexcallow/.agents/skills`
- `r1` = `/Users/alexcallow/.codex/skills/.system`
- `r2` = `/Users/alexcallow/.codex/plugins/cache/egm/egm/0.1.1/skills`
- `r3` = `/Users/alexcallow/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-bundled`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r1/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: API first-timers, Codex/Work Q&A. If the user already has an OpenAI API integration, skip this skill for API questions and use the developer docs. Read this skill before answering how Codex or ChatGPT Work behaves, where to find a feature, or how to configure or troubleshoot this app or coding agent. This includes conversation history, model and cache behavior, instruction precedence, permissions, and tool availability. Skip action requests, such as scheduling an automation, and tasks fully answered by supplied text or data. (file: r1/openai-docs/SKILL.md)

(file: r0/apollo-client/SKILL.md)
- built-in-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Codex desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Codex's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It is not for Codex in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (file: r0/synced/31fc0c17-6ddd-4792-886e-5cbd4fcd4b6f_1f3233f3-c0e3-424e-a407-80f78eb29aa1/built-in-browser/SKILL.md)
- chrome-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses Codex in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. ---
name: egm-inventive-catalyst
description: Inventive problem-solving Goldfish persona applying TRIZ principles to identify and eliminate system-level contradictions without compromise.
license: Apache-2.0
---

# Core Mandates (Universal Goldfish Context)

You are a specialized Goldfish subagent operating within the Elephant-Goldfish Model. You have been delegated a specific task by the root agent (the Elephant).

1. **Strict Read-Only Protocol**: You are a strictly read-only agent. You have NO tools to modify the workspace, write files, or compile code. Do not attempt to fix or refactor any code.
2. **Stateless Mindset (Goldfish Isolation)**: You evaluate plans with zero conversational history or external assumptions. You must read the document as a naive team member or fresh reader who has just joined the project.
3. **No Chitchat**: Avoid conversational filler. Focus exclusively on technical rationale and findings. Do not narrate your tool usage.

---

# Role

You are **Inventive Catalyst Goldfish**.
You are an expert in applying TRIZ (Theory of Inventive Problem Solving) principles to software architecture.
Your mission is to identify where proposed designs prematurely surrender to false compromises or technical contradictions (e.g., "higher throughput requires sacrificing durability", "extensibility requires complex hierarchies"). You uncover hidden contradictions and suggest established software architecture patterns to resolve them.

Crucial System Boundaries:
- Theoretical invariants are immutable system bounds, not technical contradictions to be eliminated.
- Every architectural pattern introduces secondary operational trade-offs; you MUST explicitly declare these trade-offs alongside every recommendation.

---

# Curated Inventive Software Patterns

Use this inlined catalog as your foundational pattern reference:

1. **Segmentation**: Divide monolithic structures into independent, decoupled units (modular packages, worker pools, sharded data).
   * *Secondary Trade-off*: Coordination overhead, interface boundary serialization.
2. **Extraction / Taking Out**: Separate cross-cutting or interfering concerns (interceptors, sidecars, out-of-process isolation).
   * *Secondary Trade-off*: Inter-process communication latency, additional operational artifacts.
3. **Preliminary Action**: Pre-compute or pre-allocate expensive resources (memoization, cache warming, connection pooling, ahead-of-time compilation).
   * *Secondary Trade-off*: Memory consumption during idle periods, initialization delay.
4. **Beforehand Cushioning**: Prepare fallback mitigations in advance (circuit breakers, stale-while-revalidate caches, bounded fallback queues).
   * *Secondary Trade-off*: Potential data staleness, fallback path maintenance.
5. **Inversion**: Invert control flow or data access (Inversion of Control, reactive streams, event-driven pull vs. push).
   * *Secondary Trade-off*: Execution indirection, harder stack-trace debuggability.
6. **Dynamics**: Adapt system characteristics dynamically based on workload (adaptive batching, autoscaling, dynamic rate limits).
   * *Secondary Trade-off*: System behavior unpredictability under boundary conditions.
7. **Blessing in Disguise**: Convert failure signals or liabilities into beneficial system actions (chaos engineering, backpressure signals, dead-letter re-routing).
   * *Secondary Trade-off*: Increased orchestration logic and queue management.
8. **Intermediary**: Decouple components using an intermediate coordinator (mediators, event buses, message queues, API gateways).
   * *Secondary Trade-off*: Extra execution hops, single point of failure without redundancy.
9. **Self-Service**: Make components autonomously self-heal or self-manage (reconciliation loops, watchdogs, self-tuning memory allocators).
   * *Secondary Trade-off*: Complex failure loops if health check logic is flawed.
10. **Cheap Dispensables**: Replace durable stateful instances with cheap, ephemeral components (stateless workers, ephemeral build containers, immutable runners).
    * *Secondary Trade-off*: Cold start latency, loss of persistent local disk state.

---

# Instructions

Inspect the `Mode` parameter specified by the caller:

## IF Mode: BRAINSTORM (Upstream Concept Ideation)
Evaluate the feature concept from an inventive contradiction-resolution perspective:
0. **Verify Contradiction Existence**: Check whether a genuine technical contradiction exists. If the architecture is already balanced and no true compromise is being accepted, explicitly output "No false compromise detected" rather than manufacturing speculative transforms.
1. **Identify Technical Contradictions**: Detect points where improving one parameter degrades another.
2. **Suggest Inventive Possibilities**: Propose 2-3 concrete software engineering patterns from the catalog that could resolve the conflict.
3. **Formulate the Ideal Final Result (IFR)**: Ask: "How could this system deliver its core function with minimal added operational overhead?"

## IF Mode: REVIEW (Document Audit - Step 5 Initial Strategic Review)
Audit the target document at the strategic, high-altitude level:
0. **Verify Contradiction Existence**: Check whether a genuine technical contradiction exists in the document. If the foundational architecture is already balanced and no false compromise is being accepted, explicitly output "No false compromise detected" rather than manufacturing speculative transforms.
1. **Audit for False Compromises**: Inspect the foundational architecture to identify where the author accepted an unexamined trade-off or bottleneck as inevitable.
2. **Declare Secondary Liabilities**: For any pattern suggested, explicitly state its operational costs and trade-offs.

## Audit Vectors:
* **Unexamined Compromises**: Accepted performance, reliability, or maintainability bottlenecks presented as unavoidable laws.
* **Tight Architectural Coupling**: Subsystems coupled together when extraction or an intermediary would eliminate contention.
* **Unhandled Failure Potential**: Error handling treated as passive logging rather than active mitigation or backpressure.

---

# Output Format

Report your findings back to the orchestrator in plain, natural language.

## Mode: BRAINSTORM Output
If no false compromise is detected, output: "No false compromise detected".
Otherwise, for each contradiction identified, include:
1. **Severity**: [Blocker | Major | Nit]
2. **Dimension**: Contradiction Elimination & Inventive Transforms
3. **Contradiction**: Parameter [X] versus Parameter [Y].
4. **Inventive Resolution Pattern**: Concrete software pattern recommendation from the catalog.
5. **Secondary Operational Trade-offs**: Anticipated operational overhead or liabilities.
6. **Ideal Final Result (IFR)**: What the self-sufficient architecture would look like.

## Mode: REVIEW Output
If no false compromise is detected, output: "No false compromise detected".
Otherwise, for each finding, include:
1. **Severity**: [Major | Nit] (Advisory findings)
2. **Affected Scope**: Section header or architectural subsystem.
3. **False Compromise**: Description of the accepted trade-off in the text.
4. **Proposed Resolution**: Concrete architectural pattern to resolve the contradiction.
5. **Secondary Liabilities**: Operational overhead or complexity introduced by the pattern.

# Bulk CSV inventory import

- **Author** — Alex Callow
- **Status** — Proposed
- **Date** — 2026-11-26

## Overview

Inventory operators can upload `inventory_frame.csv` from the running application and see the result as the job progresses. A routine update changes only the frames named in the file. An authoritative snapshot can also retire missing frames within a declared area of the inventory. Every accepted change is visible in frame history.

## The Problem

The application supports individual frame edits, but operators receive inventory updates as CSV files. Applying a file by hand is slow and makes it difficult to identify which rows failed. An older export can also conflict with a newer edit or omit frames that were created after the export. Operators need to apply the file, see what was accepted or skipped, and understand why a frame changed.

## Goals

- Let an authorized operator upload the supplied 45-field CSV from the application and see job progress, final counts, and actionable row errors.
- Apply `DELTA` by default. Leave absent frames alone, preserve newer edits unless the operator explicitly forces a conflicting change, and avoid duplicate frame versions and events on retry or re-upload of unchanged rows.
- Support `FULL_SNAPSHOT` for a single declared scope. Require country and region for environment-level scopes. Protect frames present in malformed rows, frames changed after the export watermark, and partitions with newer snapshots. Prevent retirement when the malformed-row rate exceeds 5% and abort before inventory writes if more than 10% of scoped active frames would retire.
- Preserve accepted versions, source timestamps, and import lineage so operators can trace updates, forced corrections, and retirements.

## Non-Goals

- Hard deletion of inventory during import.
- Arbitrary CSV schemas, field mapping, or automatic repair of malformed values.
- A single snapshot covering several separately named scopes in the first release. Operators can submit separate regional snapshots or use `DELTA` for a cross-region update.

## Technical Plan (Architecture)

### Upload and dispatch

```text
Operator → web app → BFF → Spring Boot → import_jobs
Operator → presigned PUT → S3 → SQS standard queue → Spring Boot → Temporal
                                   SQS retries → DLQ → dispatch reconciler
Temporal worker → pinned S3 object → PostgreSQL staging → inventory apply
Inventory apply → frame versions + job outcome
Operator ← web app ← BFF ← Spring Boot job status and row errors
```

The job creation API takes the import mode, optional snapshot scope and export watermark, and explicit force flag. Spring Boot validates the requested scope and permissions, creates an AWAITING_UPLOAD job, and returns its ID and the presigned PUT details through the BFF. The upload key is uploads/{jobId}/inventory_frame.csv. Use a create-only PUT and persist the accepted S3 object version so all retries read the same bytes. Expose job status, counts, fatal errors, and paginated row errors through the BFF.

Configure S3 to send object-created notifications for the uploads/ prefix directly to a standard SQS queue in the same AWS Region. Grant the bucket permission to publish through a queue policy scoped to the bucket ARN and owner account. The Spring Boot consumer handles the native S3 notification envelope, recognizes the S3 test event, and processes each object record. It decodes the key and verifies the bucket, key, object version, and size, then conditionally records PENDING and starts Temporal workflow csv-import-{jobId}. Duplicate or out-of-order records must preserve the existing object binding and job state. Acknowledge the message after each applicable record has been handled, including confirming successful or already-completed workflow dispatch. If processing a later record fails, replay of earlier records uses the same job and workflow identities. Retry with backoff. Before a DLQ event can fail a job, reconcile ambiguous workflow starts and check that the job is still dispatchable. Reconcile old AWAITING_UPLOAD and PENDING jobs against S3 and Temporal.

### Staging and validation

Accept files up to 10 MiB and 10,000 data rows, whichever limit is reached first. Verify object size before dispatch and enforce both limits while streaming. The header does not count. Exceeding either limit fails the job before inventory writes. Keep uploaded object versions and row diagnostics for 7 days. Keep the minimal durable job outcome and import lineage available to history after diagnostics expire. Bound retries and reconciliation within the object retention period.

Interpret the CSV created_date and modified_date fields as UTC at their supplied precision. Use UTC for source_modified_at storage and explicitly interpret the existing offset-free PostgreSQL column as UTC regardless of the database session timezone. Convert source timestamps to instants for watermark and manual-edit comparisons.

The Temporal worker reads the pinned object and streams logical CSV records into job- and attempt-scoped UNLOGGED staging. Heartbeats report progress and let the worker detect cancellation. Keep the EOF completion marker in the same unlogged storage as the data. Before apply, check the marker and staged counts. If a crash leaves staging incomplete or empty, reload from S3. Store row errors with stable job, row, and error keys for retries. Track identifiable frame IDs independently of row validity. Hash canonical typed frame values with SHA-256 over a versioned, ordered encoding. Preserve meaningful text, normalize typed numeric values by value, encode null distinctly, order external references by type, and preserve the position of links. Exclude job metadata, version validity, and source timestamps from the payload hash. Compare hashes using the same encoding version. After staging, reject every row for a frame ID that appears more than once, report DUPLICATE_FRAME_ID for each duplicate row, and keep the ID in the snapshot presence set. Count each rejected logical record once toward the malformed-row threshold, even if it has several validation errors.

### Inventory and history

Use the existing frame table for stable identity and frame_version for current and historical values. Resolve region, town, postcode, and format through existing lookup tables. Attach external references and ordered links to the resulting frame version. Add job, row error, scope watermark, and import lineage storage through Flyway. Map the complete CSV to the existing model, including site and spec fields on frame_version. The BFF, protobuf service definitions, Spring service, and worker need changes for job creation, progress, and application.

Re-read the current version under the existing stable-frame lock. A newer source timestamp creates a version. Equal timestamp and hash is a no-op. Skip and report stale rows and same-timestamp collisions unless forceOverwrite is authorized and set, and record both hashes for collisions. Manual writes set source_modified_at from database statement time after locking, and CSV writes preserve the input timestamp. For existing manual versions that inherited their source timestamp, use the version’s valid_from as the effective conflict baseline. Identify those versions at migration time and preserve the original source_modified_at for history. Forced corrections record FORCED_OVERWRITE and import_job_id. Subsequent imports compare against the current version’s source timestamp, including when a forced overwrite moves that timestamp backward. For example, an 11:00 row is newer after a forced overwrite replaces a 12:00 version with a 10:00 version. Use the same database-generated boundary for closing and opening a version, strictly later than the previous valid_from.

When a frame has no current version and its latest version was closed by MANUAL_DELETE, require an authorized forceOverwrite to restore it in either import mode. Without that flag, skip the row and record MANUALLY_DELETED in the job’s row errors. With it, append a new current version, preserve the CSV source timestamp, and record FORCED_OVERWRITE and import_job_id in the apply transaction. Compare and restore under the stable-frame lock.

Promote a complete staging attempt in one transaction. Acquire the job lock and verify eligibility before writing. Use one source candidate per target key and MERGE RETURNING where it fits. Close current versions and append replacements in separate set-based statements. Commit inventory, versioned references and links, the applicable scope watermark, and job result together. If the worker loses the commit response, return the stored result when it retries.

### Snapshot apply

Keep staging outside the inventory lock. During promotion, take a shared transaction-scoped inventory lock for manual writes and DELTA and an exclusive lock for FULL_SNAPSHOT. Obtain frame locks in stable ID order. Evaluate scope membership, watermark checks, and retirement against the protected pre-apply view.

Require scope to be GLOBAL or a canonical country, country/region, or country/region/environment path. Use the explicit snapshot_as_of where available, otherwise derive it from MAX(modified_date) on the complete file. Check freshness and reject watermarks below the greatest committed value for the scope or its ancestors. A broader snapshot can still apply its present rows under the ordinary conflict rules when a descendant has a newer watermark. Protect that entire descendant subtree from retirement.

Before writing inventory, fail the entire snapshot for a header-only file, an incomplete export, or an unrecoverable CSV parse error. Also fail the snapshot if any row has no recoverable frame ID or any record is outside the declared scope. Keep job diagnostics and leave inventory and the scope watermark unchanged. Count any identifiable frame ID in the CSV as present, including when other fields are malformed. Among absent active frames, exclude protected child scopes and current versions whose valid_from or source_modified_at exceeds the export watermark. Record SKIPPED_RETIREMENT_NEWER_THAN_SNAPSHOT for the latter. If eligible retirements exceed 10% of all active frames in the declared scope, fail before inventory writes. If more than 5% of CSV rows are malformed, fail the entire snapshot before writing inventory. Keep the job diagnostics and leave the scope watermark unadvanced. Represent each accepted retirement with a new RETIRED version and MISSING_FROM_FULL_SNAPSHOT. Advance only the incoming scope watermark on a successful commit.

Exclude snapshot-retired frames from the default inventory list. Expose them through an explicit retired filter, direct lookup, and frame history.

A FULL_SNAPSHOT can reactivate an unchanged row when the current version was retired with MISSING_FROM_FULL_SNAPSHOT, the incoming export watermark is strictly later than that retirement version’s valid_from, and the row’s source timestamp and canonical payload hash match the last live version. Append a new live version in the apply transaction. Apply normal conflict rules to other rows and to DELTA imports.

## Alternatives Considered

### Forward S3 notifications through Lambda

A Lambda bridge can normalize events or route them to several destinations. The import has a single queue, and Spring Boot can consume the native event. The bridge adds a deployment and another delivery failure path.

**Rejected by author** — Send S3 notifications directly to the standard SQS queue to remove the forwarding hop.

### Use logged staging

Logged staging can survive a PostgreSQL restart or failover and avoids downloading and parsing the same object again after staging is lost. It adds write-ahead logging and storage work for intermediate rows. The initial design uses UNLOGGED staging with replay from the pinned S3 object. Measure the cost of both approaches at the maximum supported upload size before committing to larger files.

### Migrate to the six-table inventory model and separate frame history

Separate site and spec entities would give those concepts independent identities and lifecycles. A migration would also change existing inventory reads and writes and would need to preserve historical values when site or spec records change.

**Rejected by author** — Extend the existing versioned schema for this release. It already gives current and historical frames one authoritative store and preserves links and external references per version. A separate history store would add a second representation of those changes.

## Detailed Implementation Plan

Deliver the operator-facing DELTA path first. Enable FULL_SNAPSHOT after measuring transaction duration and verifying retirement safeguards against the supplied CSV and concurrent writers.

1. Add the import storage and schema invariants.

   - Create [V3__create_inventory_import.sql](../../src/backend/src/main/resources/db/migration/V3__create_inventory_import.sql) for import_jobs, import_row_errors, staging rows and completion markers, scope watermarks, and import provenance on frame versions. Enforce one accepted object version per job, valid scope shape, and stable row error keys. Keep staging rows and their completion marker unlogged, with indexes for job/attempt and presence checks. Keep the durable job result separate.
   - Update [frame-inventory-schema.md](../../docs/frame-inventory-schema/frame-inventory-schema.md) to document source timestamps, interval boundaries, collision handling, retirement, and force-only restoration after manual deletion.

2. Add the backend job and worker entry points.

   Backend Java paths below are relative to [src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory](../../src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory).

   - Modify [build.gradle](../../src/backend/build.gradle) for the AWS, Temporal, and CSV parsing dependencies. Modify [application.yml](../../src/backend/src/main/resources/application.yml) to configure bucket, queue, DLQ, Temporal namespace and task queue, retry and upload settings, and worker enablement.
   - Create [inventory_import.proto](../../src/backend/src/main/proto/frameinventory/v1/inventory_import.proto) for the creation request, required signed PUT headers, status and counts, and paginated row errors. Add inventory import messages and RPCs without changing existing frame RPCs.
   - Create `inventoryimport/ImportGrpcService.java` to validate RPC requests, pass operator identity to the job service, and return job status and row diagnostics. Create `inventoryimport/ImportJobService.java` to authorize the requested mode and force flag, validate canonical scope, create the job, and sign the exact S3 PUT. Create `inventoryimport/ImportJobRepository.java` for conditional job transitions, object binding, diagnostics, and returned outcomes.
   - Create `inventoryimport/ImportDispatch.java` to decode the S3 envelope, handle test events, reconcile stale jobs, start Temporal idempotently, and handle DLQ outcomes without regressing running or completed jobs. Keep queue acknowledgment at the message boundary.
   - Create `inventoryimport/CsvImportWorkflow.java` and `inventoryimport/CsvImportActivities.java` to sequence staging and promotion, configure bounded retries and heartbeats, and record terminal failures. Register the dispatcher and worker through `inventoryimport/ImportConfiguration.java` so the application can run without AWS/Temporal import wiring when imports are disabled.
   - Create `inventoryimport/InventoryCsvReader.java` to parse CSV logical records, recover IDs where possible, validate typed fields, and build canonical hashes. Create `inventoryimport/ImportStagingRepository.java` to write batches, fence loader attempts, and publish and validate the completion marker. Keep row error persistence idempotent across restaging.
   - Create `inventoryimport/ImportApplyRepository.java` for the set-based transaction and eligibility checks. Reserve stable IDs, lock them in order, and re-read current versions before evaluating the timestamp/hash rules. Resolve existing dimensions, close and append versions, copy or replace versioned children as appropriate, and persist the final job outcome with the inventory changes. Measure guards before mutation, including scope completeness, empty snapshots, malformed percentage, watermark checks, and retirement percentage.
   - Modify `frame/FrameRepository.java` and `frame/FrameService.java` to coordinate manual writes with the shared inventory lock and set manual source timestamps after locking. Keep the current close/open interval invariant, and verify manual deletion history and restoration through imports. Implement default retirement filtering in list queries and add the retired filter to [frames.proto](../../src/backend/src/main/proto/frameinventory/v1/frames.proto), `frame/FrameGrpcService.java`, [frames.gql](../../src/bff/schema/frames.gql), [frames.ts](../../src/bff/src/resolvers/frames.ts), [frame-client.ts](../../src/bff/src/frame-client.ts), and the inventory list in [page.tsx](../../src/frontend/src/app/page.tsx). Preserve direct and history lookups.

3. Wire the application through the BFF and frontend.

   - Create [inventory-import.gql](../../src/bff/schema/inventory-import.gql) for job creation, status, and row-error types. Update [query.gql](../../src/bff/schema/query.gql) and [codegen.yml](../../src/bff/codegen.yml) where needed to expose the new operations and generated types.
   - Create [inventory-import-client.ts](../../src/bff/src/inventory-import-client.ts) for the import RPC client and [inventory-import.ts](../../src/bff/src/resolvers/inventory-import.ts) for GraphQL resolvers. Update [server.ts](../../src/bff/src/server.ts) and [index.ts](../../src/bff/src/index.ts) for schema, resolver, and client wiring. Preserve request correlation and authorization context.
   - Modify [page.tsx](../../src/frontend/src/app/page.tsx) to expose the upload entry point. Create [inventory-import.tsx](../../src/frontend/src/app/inventory-import.tsx) to collect mode and scope, submit the presigned PUT with its required headers, poll the job, and show progress and errors. Update [globals.css](../../src/frontend/src/app/globals.css) for the upload and results UI.

4. Provision and document deployment.

   - Create `infra/inventory-import/versions.tf` for Terraform and AWS provider requirements, `infra/inventory-import/variables.tf` for environment inputs, `infra/inventory-import/main.tf` to provision same-region S3 and SQS, a DLQ and redrive policy, queue publish policy scoped to the source bucket and account, and the IAM policies for signing, reading the accepted object, and consuming the queues. Create `infra/inventory-import/outputs.tf` for the bucket name, queue URLs, and application policy ARN. Commit the generated `infra/inventory-import/.terraform.lock.hcl` to pin provider selection. Use `infra/inventory-import/README.md` to document environment-specific remote state and locking, provisioning order, and Spring Boot configuration from those outputs. Enable bucket versioning and configure the seven-day upload lifecycle, including noncurrent versions. Add diagnostic cleanup to the existing import job reconciliation schedule. Preserve job summaries and lineage when deleting row diagnostics. Configure S3 CORS for the frontend origin and the signed PUT headers. Document the deployed resources, local test path, and failover/reconciliation procedure in [src/backend/README.md](../../src/backend/README.md) and the operator flow in [README.md](../../README.md).

3. **Preliminary Action**: Pre-compute or pre-allocate expensive resources (memoization, cache warming, connection pooling, ahead-of-time compilation).

4. **Beforehand Cushioning**: Prepare fallback mitigations in advance (circuit breakers, stale-while-revalidate caches, bounded fallback queues).
   * *Secondary Trade-off*: Potential data staleness, fallback path maintenance.
5. **Inversion**: Invert control flow or data access (Inversion of Control, reactive streams, event-driven pull vs. push).
   * *Secondary Trade-off*: Execution indirection, harder stack-trace debuggability.
6. **Dynamics**: Adapt system characteristics dynamically based on workload (adaptive batching, autoscaling, dynamic rate limits).

7. **Blessing in Disguise**: Convert failure signals or liabilities into beneficial system actions (chaos engineering, backpressure signals, dead-letter re-routing).

8. **Intermediary**: Decouple components using an intermediate coordinator (mediators, event buses, message queues, API gateways).

9. **Self-Service**: Make components autonomously self-heal or self-manage (reconciliation loops, watchdogs, self-tuning memory allocators).

                                   SQS retries → DLQ → dispatch reconciler
Temporal worker → pinned S3 object → PostgreSQL staging → inventory apply
Inventory apply → frame versions + job outcome
Operator ← web app ← BFF ← Spring Boot job status and row errors
```

The job creation API takes the import mode, optional snapshot scope and export watermark, and explicit force flag. Spring Boot validates the requested scope and permissions, creates an AWAITING_UPLOAD job, and returns its ID and the presigned PUT details through the BFF. The upload key is uploads/{jobId}/inventory_frame.csv. Use a create-only PUT and persist the accepted S3 object version so all retries read the same bytes. Expose job status, counts, fatal errors, and paginated row errors through the BFF.

Configure S3 to send object-created notifications for the uploads/ prefix directly to a standard SQS queue in the same AWS Region. Grant the bucket permission to publish through a queue policy scoped to the bucket ARN and owner account. The Spring Boot consumer handles the native S3 notification envelope, recognizes the S3 test event, and processes each object record. It decodes the key and verifies the bucket, key, object version, and size, then conditionally records PENDING and starts Temporal workflow csv-import-{jobId}. Duplicate or out-of-order records must preserve the existing object binding and job state. Acknowledge the message after each applicable record has been handled, including confirming successful or already-completed workflow dispatch. If processing a later record fails, replay of earlier records uses the same job and workflow identities. Retry with backoff. Before a DLQ event can fail a job, reconcile ambiguous workflow starts and check that the job is still dispatchable. Reconcile old AWAITING_UPLOAD and PENDING jobs against S3 and Temporal.

### Staging and validation

Accept files up to 10 MiB and 10,000 data rows, whichever limit is reached first. Verify object size before dispatch and enforce both limits while streaming. The header does not count. Exceeding either limit fails the job before inventory writes. Keep uploaded object versions and row diagnostics for 7 days. Keep the minimal durable job outcome and import lineage available to history after diagnostics expire. Bound retries and reconciliation within the object retention period.

Interpret the CSV created_date and modified_date fields as UTC at their supplied precision. Use UTC for source_modified_at storage and explicitly interpret the existing offset-free PostgreSQL column as UTC regardless of the database session timezone. Convert source timestamps to instants for watermark and manual-edit comparisons.

The Temporal worker reads the pinned object and streams logical CSV records into job- and attempt-scoped UNLOGGED staging. Heartbeats report progress and let the worker detect cancellation. Keep the EOF completion marker in the same unlogged storage as the data. Before apply, check the marker and staged counts. If a crash leaves staging incomplete or empty, reload from S3. Store row errors with stable job, row, and error keys for retries. Track identifiable frame IDs independently of row validity. Hash canonical typed frame values with SHA-256 over a versioned, ordered encoding. Preserve meaningful text, normalize typed numeric values by value, encode null distinctly, order external references by type, and preserve the position of links. Exclude job metadata, version validity, and source timestamps from the payload hash. Compare hashes using the same encoding version. After staging, reject every row for a frame ID that appears more than once, report DUPLICATE_FRAME_ID for each duplicate row, and keep the ID in the snapshot presence set. Count each rejected logical record once toward the malformed-row threshold, even if it has several validation errors.

### Inventory and history

Use the existing frame table for stable identity and frame_version for current and historical values. Resolve region, town, postcode, and format through existing lookup tables. Attach external references and ordered links to the resulting frame version. Add job, row error, scope watermark, and import lineage storage through Flyway. Map the complete CSV to the existing model, including site and spec fields on frame_version. The BFF, protobuf service definitions, Spring service, and worker need changes for job creation, progress, and application.

Re-read the current version under the existing stable-frame lock. A newer source timestamp creates a version. Equal timestamp and hash is a no-op. Skip and report stale rows and same-timestamp collisions unless forceOverwrite is authorized and set, and record both hashes for collisions. Manual writes set source_modified_at from database statement time after locking, and CSV writes preserve the input timestamp. For existing manual versions that inherited their source timestamp, use the version’s valid_from as the effective conflict baseline. Identify those versions at migration time and preserve the original source_modified_at for history. Forced corrections record FORCED_OVERWRITE and import_job_id. Subsequent imports compare against the current version’s source timestamp, including when a forced overwrite moves that timestamp backward. For example, an 11:00 row is newer after a forced overwrite replaces a 12:00 version with a 10:00 version. Use the same database-generated boundary for closing and opening a version, strictly later than the previous valid_from.

When a frame has no current version and its latest version was closed by MANUAL_DELETE, require an authorized forceOverwrite to restore it in either import mode. Without that flag, skip the row and record MANUALLY_DELETED in the job’s row errors. With it, append a new current version, preserve the CSV source timestamp, and record FORCED_OVERWRITE and import_job_id in the apply transaction. Compare and restore under the stable-frame lock.

Promote a complete staging attempt in one transaction. Acquire the job lock and verify eligibility before writing. Use one source candidate per target key and MERGE RETURNING where it fits. Close current versions and append replacements in separate set-based statements. Commit inventory, versioned references and links, the applicable scope watermark, and job result together. If the worker loses the commit response, return the stored result when it retries.

### Snapshot apply

Keep staging outside the inventory lock. During promotion, take a shared transaction-scoped inventory lock for manual writes and DELTA and an exclusive lock for FULL_SNAPSHOT. Obtain frame locks in stable ID order. Evaluate scope membership, watermark checks, and retirement against the protected pre-apply view.

Require scope to be GLOBAL or a canonical country, country/region, or country/region/environment path. Use the explicit snapshot_as_of where available, otherwise derive it from MAX(modified_date) on the complete file. Check freshness and reject watermarks below the greatest committed value for the scope or its ancestors. A broader snapshot can still apply its present rows under the ordinary conflict rules when a descendant has a newer watermark. Protect that entire descendant subtree from retirement.

Before writing inventory, fail the entire snapshot for a header-only file, an incomplete export, or an unrecoverable CSV parse error. Also fail the snapshot if any row has no recoverable frame ID or any record is outside the declared scope. Keep job diagnostics and leave inventory and the scope watermark unchanged. Count any identifiable frame ID in the CSV as present, including when other fields are malformed. Among absent active frames, exclude protected child scopes and current versions whose valid_from or source_modified_at exceeds the export watermark. Record SKIPPED_RETIREMENT_NEWER_THAN_SNAPSHOT for the latter. If eligible retirements exceed 10% of all active frames in the declared scope, fail before inventory writes. If more than 5% of CSV rows are malformed, fail the entire snapshot before writing inventory. Keep the job diagnostics and leave the scope watermark unadvanced. Represent each accepted retirement with a new RETIRED version and MISSING_FROM_FULL_SNAPSHOT. Advance only the incoming scope watermark on a successful commit.

Exclude snapshot-retired frames from the default inventory list. Expose them through an explicit retired filter, direct lookup, and frame history.

A FULL_SNAPSHOT can reactivate an unchanged row when the current version was retired with MISSING_FROM_FULL_SNAPSHOT, the incoming export watermark is strictly later than that retirement version’s valid_from, and the row’s source timestamp and canonical payload hash match the last live version. Append a new live version in the apply transaction. Apply normal conflict rules to other rows and to DELTA imports.

## Alternatives Considered

### Forward S3 notifications through Lambda

A Lambda bridge can normalize events or route them to several destinations. The import has a single queue, and Spring Boot can consume the native event. The bridge adds a deployment and another delivery failure path.

**Rejected by author** — Send S3 notifications directly to the standard SQS queue to remove the forwarding hop.

### Use logged staging

Logged staging can survive a PostgreSQL restart or failover and avoids downloading and parsing the same object again after staging is lost. It adds write-ahead logging and storage work for intermediate rows. The initial design uses UNLOGGED staging with replay from the pinned S3 object. Measure the cost of both approaches at the maximum supported upload size before committing to larger files.

### Migrate to the six-table inventory model and separate frame history

Separate site and spec entities would give those concepts independent identities and lifecycles. A migration would also change existing inventory reads and writes and would need to preserve historical values when site or spec records change.

**Rejected by author** — Extend the existing versioned schema for this release. It already gives current and historical frames one authoritative store and preserves links and external references per version. A separate history store would add a second representation of those changes.

# Codex integration

## Install and locate the plugin

For the desktop app, install the [published EGM plugin](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugins_6aeb90f47ec88191a3c107e01d3eb357). This listing is desktop-only.

For Codex CLI, install the whole plugin, including its personas and standards:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add google/elephant-goldfish-model
codex plugin add egm@egm
```

Start a fresh session after installation. Select the installed `egm` skill
from the available skills. Use its discovered absolute `SKILL.md` path;
do not assume a particular cache directory, version, or checkout location.

From `<plugin>/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`, the plugin root is three parent
directories above the file. Resolve bundled `agents/`, `resources/`, and
`docs/` paths against that root. Resolve `references/` against the active
skill's directory. Resolve user documents and generated artifacts against
the user's working directory. Never substitute similarly named files in the
user's project for bundled personas or standards.

If the user's prompt or agent instructions file (`AGENTS.md`) has a line
`EGM artifact directory: <path>`, write briefs, drafts, and reports to that
folder. Resolve a relative path against the working directory. If a path from
`AGENTS.md` resolves outside the working directory, after following symbolic
links, ask the user to confirm it before creating the folder or writing there.
If they decline or no one can confirm, use the working directory and say why.
Create the folder if it does not exist.

In ChatGPT Work, a skill may be exposed through a cloud resource identifier
while supporting files live in the installed local bundle. Use the installed
path supplied by the skill inventory or installation metadata for those files;
do not construct cloud resource identifiers for arbitrary supporting paths.
If no installed path is available, report the missing capability instead of
guessing a cache location. Read reviewer filenames and frontmatter from the
bundle: a role such as `egm-design` maps to `agents/design_critic.md`, not
`agents/design.md`. Confirm each resolved path before dispatch.

## Fresh-context reviewers

Inspect the available native subagent tool schema. Tool names can be
namespaced and vary by Codex version. When `spawn_agent` exposes
`fork_context`, explicitly set `fork_context: false` for every Goldfish.
When the schema instead exposes `fork_turns`, use `fork_turns: "none"`.
This applies to reviewers launched by a synthesizer too. Use a general-purpose agent
and pass absolute paths to the persona, standards, target document, and
explicitly selected reading list. Do not pass the parent transcript, private
reasoning, or answers the document is supposed to explain.

Require the reviewer to read its persona, target, and every supplied standard
before returning findings. A missing read or inaccessible file is an incomplete
review, not a clean result. Verify native tool results when the host exposes
them; a parent-written completion summary is not equivalent evidence.

Wait for actual reviewer completion before synthesizing findings. Propagate
failures and timeouts; a launched reviewer is not a completed review. If
nesting is unavailable, dispatch reviewers directly from the parent while
preserving the same isolation. If the available tool cannot establish a fresh
context, stop the Goldfish review and report that limitation.

Fresh conversation context does not isolate the filesystem, configured memory
services, or project instructions. Do not retrieve conversation history or
memory to supply missing design context. An isolation test should use a unique
parent-only marker and check the actual child result, not the parent's claim.

The `fork_context: false` and `fork_turns: "none"` options concern parent
conversation turns. They do not prove that Codex excludes host instruction
files. Issue [#237](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/237)
reports that Codex CLI 0.166.0 injected project and user `AGENTS.md` files
despite `fork_turns: "none"`. Treat instruction-file exclusion as unverified
unless a separate child-context probe confirms it for the tested host version.

## Questions and artifacts

The shared skills' question payloads describe the intended interaction, not a
literal Codex API. Use a structured question tool only when it is available
and permitted in the current mode, mapping to its actual schema. Otherwise
ask one plain-text question and wait for the answer. Preserve the skill's
readiness and section approval gates; tool unavailability is not approval.

Link generated artifacts with absolute-path Markdown links such as
`[design draft](/absolute/project/design_draft.md)`. For paths containing
spaces use `[design draft](</absolute/my project/design_draft.md>)`.
Do not use `file://` links in Codex chat.

## Verification

Run the offline packaging checks with `pytest tests/unit`. The opt-in native
workflow tests are documented in [TESTING.md](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/blob/main/TESTING.md). They require
an authenticated Codex CLI and consume model usage. Installing or discovering
the plugin alone does not establish end-to-end workflow support.

## ChatGPT

Install the [published EGM plugin](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugins_6aeb90f47ec88191a3c107e01d3eb357) in the ChatGPT desktop app. This listing is desktop-only; it does not establish support for cloud Work sessions.

### Test a local package

For personal testing, open Plugins > Add > Upload plugin archive in ChatGPT.
Package the runtime files from the repository root:

```sh
python3 scripts/pack_plugin.py --target openai --output /tmp/egm-chatgpt
```

Use a fresh output directory. Upload `/tmp/egm-chatgpt/egm-openai.zip` and
install the plugin in the ChatGPT desktop app. Use
**Try in chat** in a new thread that runs locally. The earlier cloud Work
test in `TESTING.md` predates this package's desktop-only declaration.
Keep repository marketplace catalogs and development files outside this archive.
The OpenAI directory package declares local execution because bootstrap uses
shell commands. Its listing uses the portable manifest's OpenAI extension;
the Codex compatibility manifest retains matching metadata for native installs.
Keep `.claude-plugin/` outside the OpenAI archive: its agent adapters belong
to the Claude Code integration. Public directory plugins cannot include hooks.

Enterprise, Business, and Edu workspaces can import the plugin via Admin > Plugins > Add > Import marketplace.
Set the repository URL to `https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model` and marketplace path to `.agents/plugins`.
Skills are accessible via `@egm` for direct interaction.
Check the native tools in the current chat before starting a Goldfish review.

# Execution Instructions

This file holds bundled execution rules shared across multiple Elephant-Goldfish
Model (EGM) skills, plus drafting-only rules used strictly by `egm-draft`. Only
apply the sections referenced by the active skill.

## Plugin-Root Resource Paths

Bundled personas (`agents/<file>.md`), standards
(`resources/document_standards/<name>.md`), harness guides (`docs/*.md`), and
this file (`resources/execution_instructions.md`) sit at the plugin root, two
directories above each skill's folder (`<plugin-root>/skills/<skill-name>/`).

*   **Local / relative path**: Read `../../resources/execution_instructions.md`
    (or `<plugin-root>/<path>`).
*   **Claude Code and Cowork**: Read
    `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/resources/execution_instructions.md` (or
    `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/<path>`).
*   **Pathless `<SKILL>` injection**: If the harness injects a skill without its
    file path, check `~/.gemini/config/plugins/egm/<path>`.

Pass spawned subagents the resolved absolute paths of their persona file and
standard when `<plugin-root>` is known. A failed skill-relative lookup does not
mean the file is absent from the plugin.
Never substitute workspace files with similar names for bundled personas,
standards, or execution instructions. If you cannot read a required plugin-root
file after resolving `<plugin-root>`, say so instead of calling it missing; apply
the active skill's inline fallback only when file tools are unavailable.

## Subagent Delegation (Goldfish Isolation)

Applies to subagent-spawning skills (`egm-bootstrap`, `egm-brainstorm`,
`egm-review`, and `egm-review-loop`):

A Goldfish runs in a fresh context with no conversation history. Spawn each
subagent with your harness's subagent tool (Antigravity: `invoke_subagent`;
Claude Code: `Agent`; Codex: `spawn_agent`). Each subagent is defined in
`agents/<file>.md`, and its frontmatter `name` (for example `egm-zoom-out`) is
the subagent type to request where your harness registers named subagents.
Otherwise spawn a general-purpose subagent and tell it to read that persona
file first. Pass prompts verbatim and wait for the report. If your harness
cannot nest subagents, use direct dispatch instead of `egm-synthesizer` (see
[harnesses.md](../docs/harnesses.md)). If your harness has no subagent tool,
follow the active skill's fallback rule (`egm-bootstrap` runs scout steps
inline; `egm-review`, `egm-brainstorm`, and `egm-review-loop` stop and tell the
user that a review in the same context is not a Goldfish review).

## Shared Design & Review Constraints

Applies strictly to `egm-brainstorm`, `egm-draft`, and `egm-review` (not
`egm-bootstrap`):

*   **Artifact-First Delivery (MANDATORY)**: You are **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN** from
    presenting large proposals, drafts, summaries, or review reports directly in
    the chat pane. Write them directly to the working directory (or your
    harness's artifact directory, if one is configured) via your file-writing
    tool, share the file path or clickable link in chat, and ask the user for
    review.
*   **Plain-English Standard**: Write concepts briefs, specs, summaries,
    reports, and communications in simple, direct, jargon-free plain English.
    Explain technical mechanisms concretely. Do not summarize away substance or
    rely on buzzwords, promotional adjectives (*seamless*, *robust*,
    *blazingly fast*), or decorative adverbs (*seamlessly*, *effortlessly*,
    *literally*, *drastically*, *obviously*).
*   **Adversarial Rigor (No Sycophancy)**: Never agree by default. Stress-test
    ideas, strategies, and opinions to find weak points, edge cases, and blind
    spots before affirming anything. Lead with what is wrong, missing, or risky
    before highlighting merits. Never parrot user framing or validate asserted
    conclusions reflexively; surface what the user is missing, the strongest
    counter-argument, and whether the opposing view holds. Only agree after
    rigorous, objective scrutiny.
    *   **Banned Adjectives (No Flattery)**: Never use validating adjectives
        like `"brilliant"`, `"great"`, `"smart"`, `"correct"`, `"perfect"`,
        `"excellent"`, or `"spot-on"` on the user's inputs, corrections, or
        decisions.
    *   **Banned Apologies**: Never output polite apologies (e.g., `"I
        apologize"`, `"I am sorry"`, `"Forgive me"`) when challenged or
        corrected. State the corrected technical logic and trade-offs directly.
*   **Interaction Invariants**: Every interactive single-select gate (structured
    question tool such as `ask_question`, if your harness has one, or plain
    chat) MUST contain strictly one question (`len(questions) == 1`), set
    `is_multi_select: false`, provide clear action-oriented options without
    `(Recommended)` prefixes, never emit a structured question call with empty
    visible chat text, and be the sole tool call in its model response step
    (finish preparatory file reads or writes in an earlier step of the turn
    first, then output visible chat text and invoke the gate alone to yield).
    Ask open-ended text inputs (such as file paths or lists) in plain chat.

Applies **strictly** during `egm-draft` (never during `egm-bootstrap`,
`egm-review`, or other workflows):

*   **Design-Only Scope**: You are strictly forbidden from
    writing, modifying, or building any production implementation files (e.g.,
    `.h`, `.cc`, `.py`, `.go`) in the source tree. You may only write code
    inside a markdown draft block or in a temporary scratchpad file.
    *   **Scratchpad Location (CRITICAL)**: You MUST write any temporary
        scratchpad code files ONLY outside the project source tree, in your
        conversation's active scratch directory or, if your harness has none,
        a new private directory created with `mktemp -d`. If neither is
        available, keep the code in a markdown draft block. Do not use fixed,
        shared paths such as `/tmp/scratch.py`. You are STRICTLY FORBIDDEN
        from creating `.h`, `.cc`, `.py`, `.go`, or any other code files
        anywhere inside the project source tree.

        and illustrative code only. Label any markdown or scratchpad example

        continue the design or leave the workflow for implementation.
